newsitem.title: FRANCE: France plans to extend period for takeover bids.
newsitem.headline: France plans to extend period for takeover bids.

text.p: France plans to extend the period during which takeover bids run to 25 days for friendly bids and 35 days for hostile bids compared to the current 20 days for both, Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday.
It also plans to reduce the threshold of share holding at which a company must declare its intentions to 10 percent from 20 percent.

The measures -- of which the first was proposed by the financial markets council, and the second by the stock market watchdog COB -- follow a call by President Jacques Chirac earlier this year to improve the conditions under which French companies can defend themselves against hostile takeover bids.
Arthuis also told a news conference that reforms to allow the launch of pension funds would be ready by the end of June.
"My objective is for everything to be in place by the end of June" he said.
